header.running_head: The Fast of Hadhrat Abu Amr Ansaari (RA)

blocks.text: in the Battles of Badr, Uhud and the pledge at Aqaba. I once saw him fasting (on the battlefield), restless because of severe thirst. He asked his slave to pass to him his shield and when the slave did so, he fired an arrow which did not go far (because he had grown weak with thirst). When he had fired three arrows, he said that he had heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Whoever fires an arrow in the path of Allaah, the arrow shall be a source of light for him on the Day of Qiyaamah whether it reaches its target or not.' Hadhrat Abu Amr (RA) was martyred before sunset of that day.
Performing Salaah While Out in the path of Allaah
The Salaah of Rasulullaah ﷺ On the Night Before the Battle of Badr was Fought

Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "There was not a single horseman amongst us during the Battle of Badr besides Miqdaad (RA). I noticed that each one of us was asleep (the night before the battle) besides Rasulullaah ﷺ. He was performing salaah beneath a tree and weeping until dawn broke."[^1]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Performs Salaah in Usfaan

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that they were with Rasulullaah ﷺ at a place called Usfaan when the Mushrikeen army under the command of Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) confronted them. The Mushrikeen army was positioned between the Muslims and the Qibla. When Rasulullaah ﷺ led the Sahabah (RA) in the Zuhr salaah, the Mushrikeen said, "If only we had taken advantage of the state of obliviousness that they were in (during their salaah) and attacked them!" However, they consoled themselves by saying, "A salaah is approaching (the Asr salaah) that is more beloved to them than their children and even their own selves (we can attack them then)." However, between the Zurh and Asr salaahs, Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS) came with the revelation of the following verses of the Qur'aan describing the Salaatul Khowf:

blocks.arabic_text: وَاِذَا كُنۡتَ فِيۡهِمۡ فَاَقَمۡتَ لَهُمُ الصَّلٰوةَ
blocks.text: When you (O Muhammad ﷺ) are with them (present with the Muslims on the battlefield) and you lead them in salaah...[^2]
A narration of Muslim from Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) states that the Mushrikeen said, "There shall soon come a salaah which is more beloved to them than even their own children."[^3]
The Salaah of Hadhrat Abbaad bin Bishr (RA) In the Path of Allaah
